blocks.text: 今天我们启动电网守护者计划（Grid Protectors Program），这是一项全国性行动，旨在让我们建设园区所在社区的居民和企业用上可负担、可靠的电力。我们将与公用事业公司、监管机构和政策制定者合作，为未来的园区制定安排，在电网承压时降低用电需求。

inlines.text: 今天我们启动
电网守护者计划
（Grid Protectors Program），这是一项全国性行动，旨在让我们建设园区所在社区的居民和企业用上可负担、可靠的电力。我们将与公用事业公司、监管机构和政策制定者合作，为未来的园区制定安排，在电网承压时降低用电需求。

blocks.text: 无论是北方寒潮来袭时供暖，还是南方热浪期间开空调，家庭都需要可靠的电力。我们的目标是让园区的灵活性成为一种资源，在社区最需要的时候供公用事业公司调用。

inlines.text: 无论是北方寒潮来袭时供暖，还是南方热浪期间开空调，家庭都需要可靠的电力。我们的目标是让园区的灵活性成为一种资源，在社区最需要的时候供公用事业公司调用。

blocks.text: 预计到2030年，美国数据中心容量将超过100吉瓦⁠（在新窗口打开），我们因此迎来一个千载难逢的机会：通过建设能在社区最需要时调整用电的园区，来强化电网。

blocks.text: 佐治亚州是我们的起点。通过电网守护者计划，我们希望让这种灵活性成为未来园区建设和运营的核心组成部分。这意味着在设计设施时就考虑在需要时降低用电，并与公用事业公司商定可削减多少需求、多快削减以及持续多久。具体安排将因地点而异，相关承诺一旦敲定，我们会另行公布。

blocks.text: 根据当地需求和可用设备，我们还将与电网运营商合作，由现场发电或储能供电，并利用电池和功率控制来平抑需求波动。

inlines.text: 根据当地需求和可用设备，我们还将与电网运营商合作，由现场发电或储能供电，并利用电池和功率控制来平抑需求波动。

blocks.text: 无论需求高低，输电线、变电站及其他电网基础设施的建设都是固定成本。通过在电网有余量时多用一些电、在电网承压时减少用电，我们可以帮助分担这些基础设施的成本，同时减少为满足峰值需求而进行昂贵升级的必要。这有助于为其他用户压低成本。

blocks.text: 美国需要更多电力来支撑经济增长，而AI正成为其中相当大的一部分需求。家庭和小企业不应被要求为计算园区的用电买单。我们始终承诺自行承担能源成本，包括我们使用的电力以及服务园区所需的基础设施。大型计算设施应当支付自身成本，并帮助公用事业公司管理它们所依赖的系统。

blocks.text: 对于计划中的埃芬汉县（Effingham County）园区，我们已承诺支付服务该项目所需的全部基础设施和电力服务成本。园区投入运营后，我们可以在需要时减少取电，帮助为其他用户保留电力。

inlines.text: 对于计划中的埃芬汉县（Effingham County）园区，我们已承诺支付服务该项目所需的全部基础设施和电力服务成本。园区投入运营后，我们可以在需要时减少取电，帮助为其他用户保留电力。

blocks.text: 我们与Georgia Power的协议还包括⁠（在新窗口打开）最高1,000兆瓦的灵活需求响应，释放出电力，帮助数十万家庭在极端高温期间维持空调运转（按平均用电量计算约70万户）。从规模上看，这相当于约70万户家庭的年均用电需求，比华盛顿特区和波士顿的家庭总数加起来还多。

blocks.text: 想象一下度假小镇上的一家餐厅。旺季时它需要足够的餐桌和厨房空间，但全年都得为这些容量付费。老顾客帮它维持使用率，在旅游淡季时帮着分摊账单。我们提议的就是做那个老顾客。

blocks.text: 电力需求也随季节起落，不同地区的用电高峰出现在不同时间。我们的计算园区全年都需要电力。有了合适的协议，这种稳定的需求可以帮助把电网的固定成本分摊到更多售电量上，而灵活性让我们能在系统最繁忙时降低需求。我们仍需承担园区产生的成本；目标是让其他用户也能受益。

blocks.text: 我们的协议也为佐治亚电力公司降低用户成本的更广泛计划做出了贡献。这家公用事业公司预计从2029年起，其大负荷协议组合及预期增长（包括 Project Camellia）每年可为用户节省约9.5亿美元⁠（在新窗口打开）。该公司估计，一个典型居民用户每月用电1,000千瓦时，每月至少可受益15美元。

blocks.text: 展望未来

inlines.text: 展望未来

blocks.text: 与佐治亚州的协议只是一个起点。在 OpenAI，通过我们的 Grid Protectors 计划，我们看到了一个机会，可以帮助社区即使在紧急和高需求时期也能保持供电。我们将与公用事业公司、监管机构和政策制定者合作，为我们未来建设的园区制定切实可行的安排——这些安排要反映当地电网需求，帮助园区在电网承压时提供支持，并承担我们产生的成本。长期合同和财务担保可以在项目延期、缩减或取消时保护其他用户。

blocks.text: 灵活性无法取代对新能源供应和输电的投资。在这些投资之外，我们的 Grid Protectors 计划可以帮助电网更可靠，并保护家庭和小企业免于承担 AI 基础设施的成本。这就是我们希望计算园区达到的标准。

blocks.text: Today we’re launching the Grid Protectors Program, a national effort to support affordable, reliable electricity for families and businesses in the communities where we build. Working with utilities, regulators and policymakers, we’ll develop arrangements for our future campuses to reduce electricity demand when the grid is under strain.

inlines.text: Today we’re launching the
Grid Protectors Program

, a national effort to support affordable, reliable electricity for families and businesses in the communities where we build. Working with utilities, regulators and policymakers, we’ll develop arrangements for our future campuses to reduce electricity demand when the grid is under strain.

blocks.text: Whether it’s heating homes during a northern cold snap or running air conditioning through a southern heat wave, families need reliable electricity. Our goal is to make campus flexibility a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most.

inlines.text: Whether it’s heating homes during a northern cold snap or running air conditioning through a southern heat wave, families need reliable electricity. Our goal is to make campus flexibility a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most.

blocks.text: With U.S. data center capacity projected to exceed 100 gigawatts by 2030⁠(opens in a new window), we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to strengthen the electric grid by building campuses that can adjust their power use when communities need it most.

inlines.text: With U.S. data center capacity projected to exceed
100 gigawatts by 2030⁠(opens in a new window)
, we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to strengthen the electric grid by building campuses that can adjust their power use when communities need it most.

blocks.text: Georgia is our starting point. Through Grid Protectors, our ambition is to make this kind of flexibility a core part of how we build and operate future campuses. That means designing facilities to reduce electricity use when needed and working with utilities to agree on how much demand can be reduced, how quickly and for how long. The arrangements will differ by location, and we will share additional commitments as they are finalized.

inlines.text: Georgia is our starting point. Through Grid Protectors, our ambition is to make this kind of flexibility a core part of how we build and operate future campuses. That means designing facilities to reduce electricity use when needed and working with utilities to agree on how much demand can be reduced, how quickly and for how long. The arrangements will differ by location, and we will share additional commitments as they are finalized.

blocks.text: Depending on local needs and the equipment available, we will also work with grid operators to supply power from on-site generation or storage, and use batteries and power controls to smooth changes in demand.

inlines.text: Depending on local needs and the equipment available, we will also work with grid operators to supply power from on-site generation or storage, and use batteries and power controls to smooth changes in demand.

blocks.text: Power lines, substations and other grid infrastructure builds are a fixed cost whether demand is low or high. By using more electricity when the grid has room and reducing our use when it is under strain, we can help pay for that infrastructure while limiting the need for costly upgrades to meet peak demand. That can help keep costs down for other customers.

blocks.text: America needs more electricity to support economic growth, and AI is becoming a significant part of that demand. Families and small businesses should not be asked to subsidize a compute campus’s electricity needs. We’ve always been committed to paying our own energy costs, including the electricity we use and the infrastructure needed to serve our campuses. Large computing facilities should pay their costs and help utilities manage the systems they depend on.

blocks.text: A model in Georgia

inlines.text: A model in Georgia

blocks.text: For our planned Effingham County campus, we have committed to pay the full infrastructure and electric-service costs required to serve the project. Once the campus is operating, we can reduce the power we draw during times of need, helping preserve electricity for other customers.

blocks.text: Our agreement with Georgia Power also includes⁠(opens in a new window) up to 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response, freeing up power to help keep air conditioning running in hundreds of thousands of homes (~700 000 households at average electricity usage) during extreme heat. For scale, that is equivalent to the average electricity demand of roughly 700,000 households. That’s more households than Washington, D.C., and Boston combined.

blocks.text: These compute facilities are much different than data centers built even a few years ago, allowing us to be flexible in our power demand.

blocks.text: This means we can turn down our demand so that families, small businesses, and other ratepayers will continue to have power. Building grid assets is expensive and Georgia Power says this flexibility can reduce the amount of new generation it needs to build to serve future growth. Although the campus is still in development, we intend for Effingham to serve as a pilot for Grid Protectors, building on an agreement that already provides a model for future campuses.

blocks.text: Imagine a restaurant in a vacation town. It needs enough tables and kitchen space for the busy season, but it has to pay for that capacity year-round. Regular customers help keep it in use and cover the bills when tourism slows. We are proposing to be that regular customer.

blocks.text: Electricity demand also rises and falls with the seasons, with different regions facing their biggest peaks at different times. Our compute campuses need power year-round. With the right agreements, that steady demand can help spread the grid’s fixed costs across more electricity sales, while flexibility lets us reduce demand when the system is busiest. We still need to pay the costs our campuses create; the goal is for other customers to benefit, too.

blocks.text: Our agreement also contributes to Georgia Power’s broader plan to lower costs for customers. The utility projects approximately $950 million in annual customer savings beginning in 2029⁠(opens in a new window) from its portfolio of large-load agreements and expected growth, including Project Camellia. It estimates a benefit of at least $15 a month for a typical residential customer using 1,000 kilowatt-hours.

blocks.text: Looking forward

inlines.text: Looking forward

blocks.text: The Georgia agreement is a starting point. At OpenAI, through our Grid Protectors program, we see an opportunity to help communities keep the lights on even in times of emergency and high demand. We will work with utilities, regulators and policymakers to develop practical arrangements for the campuses we build in the future-arrangements that reflect local grid needs, help campuses support the grid when it is under pressure, and pay the costs we create. Long-term contracts and financial assurances can protect other customers if a project is delayed, reduced or canceled.

blocks.text: Flexibility cannot replace investment in new energy supply and transmission. Alongside those investments, our Grid Protectors program can help make the grid more reliable and protect families and small businesses from bearing the costs of AI infrastructure. That is the standard we want our compute campuses to meet.
